quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks only.
Trucks are entering the highway.
A steep hill is coming.
Trucks have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is coming.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers that a steep hill is ahead. Slow down to drive safely.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: How fast you might drive in this area.
The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
How fast to drive in heavy traffic.
How fast to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are legally allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum and minimum speeds allowed on that road. The maximum speeds are for good conditions. You must drive slower when the weather or road conditions are bad.

questions.question: Two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
The vehicle on the right must let the vehicle on the left go first.
Drivers should use hand signals to talk to each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before you turn or change lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before you turn or change lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Check if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What are highway signs called when they warn about dangerous conditions?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to possible dangers ahead. Follow these signs for your safety. Ignoring a warning sign could cause an accident.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross these lines to turn left into or out of a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits only.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and carpool vehicles only.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits only.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When you are entering a street from a garage or alley.
When a car on your left reaches an unmarked intersection at the same time as you.
When your traffic light is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if children were not present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a crossing guard, sign, or police officer. Drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
You can drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Use low beams, not high beams. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe passing on a two-way street requires three things: you can see the road ahead clearly, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you will need to use extra force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before using the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. When stopping, ease off the gas first to slow down, then apply steady brake pressure. This helps prevent rear-end collisions.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: On an uphill slope, leave more space in front of your vehicle. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space reduces the chance of a collision.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers your plans.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are out, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then proceed with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly they may seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly they may seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that they appear to be drunk. Opening a window, playing loud music, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver safe.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what lights should you use?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use parking lights only.
Use headlights only.
Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and leave low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: When stopped at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on. This makes sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road ahead has a sharp curve (in this case, to the right). Slow down before the curve, just as you would at a sharp turn.

questions.question: Which of these helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows painted in lanes show which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver who arrives first.
The driver who arrives last.
One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrives first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, all drivers must stop. The first driver to reach the intersection goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going in the same direction. You may cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats made for their size. No adult is strong enough to safely hold a child during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper car seat for young children.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Fill your tires to the correct pressure.
Slow down when it is raining.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires in good condition, fill them to the correct pressure, and slow down in the rain. Hydroplaning happens more often at higher speeds.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on your path until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
Cannot turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer need to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in that direction. However, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass first.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
Only during daylight hours.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: As a general rule, you can cross broken lines but not solid lines. Solid yellow lines may only be crossed when you are turning.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway:

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Exit at the next exit and come back.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit at the next exit and come back.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to emergencies.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe pace.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to emergencies.
questions.explanation: The only way to have enough time to react to mistakes by other drivers is to leave plenty of space between your vehicle and the vehicles around you.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Find a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no train is coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turn yield on green.
One-way.
Cattle crossing.
Two-way left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn yield on green.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they can turn left on a green light. However, they must first yield to any oncoming traffic. Complete the turn only when it is safe.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions while driving. Any task that takes your attention away from driving is dangerous. Keep your full focus on the road.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
Even if it means driving off the pavement.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available passing lane.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right if the vehicle ahead is turning left or waiting to turn left and a passing lane is available. You can also pass on the right on a road with two or more lanes in the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches you, what must you do?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights, sirens, or warning devices, move to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed frequently to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic and stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because other vehicles are unlikely to be coming.
By using the highway shoulder.
If your lane is next to a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never drive on the highway shoulder to pass. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?

options.text: A steady green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you. You have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Two solid white lines mark a crosswalk. As a driver, you should know that:

options.text: Vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.
You must give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
Pedestrians must stay out of the way of all traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must give pedestrians in crosswalks the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Crosswalk lines show where pedestrians should cross. You must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians of danger. Sound it if you think another driver might hit you.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Slow down to reduce the risk.
